rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 99, Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 1: "Enter the total interest you paid in 2025 on qualified student loans ... Don't enter more than $2,500"; p. 98, "Don't include any amount paid from a distribution of earnings made from a qualified tuition program". Both take the interest less the unqualified and the assisted amounts, floored at zero, capped at $2,500 (subtracting the two in turn with a zero floor equals subtracting their sum), and both refuse on sa.excluded_income. The project asks sli.unqualified_any and sli.assisted_any only after sli.any; the reply reads them directly. executable triage (.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json, executable-triage-v2): 2,643 of 2,726 agree; 83 candidate-unknown (20 completed, e.g. classm.eic.1: no student loan, project $0), no value difference. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 99, Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 1, and p970 p. 33, Don't Include as Interest and No Double Benefit Allowed. Both take the interest less the unqualified amount (now including a loan the filer was not legally obligated to pay) and less the assisted amount (now including interest an employer paid under an educational assistance program), floored at zero and capped at $2,500; subtracting the two in turn with a zero floor equals subtracting their sum. The project asks the exclusions only after sli.any on a return not married filing separately (sli.any_if_not_mfs); the reply reads them directly, and the deduction is zero on a separate return under both. Same point as the earlier rulings on this line. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 99, Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 1, "Enter the total interest you paid in 2025 on qualified student loans ... Don't enter more than $2,500". As ruled on 2026-11-14, -15 and -17: both take the interest less the unqualified and assisted amounts, floored at zero and capped at $2,500 (subtracting the two in turn from a zero-floored amount equals subtracting their sum); the project asks sli.any only on a return that is not married filing separately (sli.any_if_not_mfs), the reply reads it on every return, and sli.unqualified_any and sli.assisted_any only after sli.any. The new item of sli.unqualified_any (study not toward a credential, or at a school that is not eligible; i1040gi p. 99) changes its wording, not this expression.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The worksheet gives no amount for married filing separately, which cannot take the deduction; the project enters zero there and the second enters $85,000. Neither reaches Schedule 1 line 21: sli.deduction is zero for married filing separately.
Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 6 is used only when line 4 is more than line 5 (line 8 skips it otherwise), where the signed difference and the floored one are the same.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project skips to zero when line 4 is not more than line 5, as the worksheet says; the second always applies the ratio, which then has a part of zero or less, and prorate keeps the ratio at 0 or more, so it also gives zero (the same argument as the classified mutant on sli.line8).
Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 8 never exceeds line 1: prorate's ratio is at most 1.000 (Lean lemma prorate_le_amount), so the floor at zero never applies.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 98, Schedule 1, line 21: the deduction is allowed only if "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, aren't claimed as a dependent on someone else's (such as your parent's) 2025 tax return." The reply drops that condition (its note says no input answers 'claimed'); the request's person collection carries person.sav_claimed, which the project counts in sli.claimed_count. Same point as the earlier rulings on this line. The review was occasioned by the reworded sli.assisted_any (employer educational assistance, p970 p. 33) and sli.unqualified_any (a loan the filer was not legally obligated to pay, p970 p. 33); the reply's exclusions match the project's on both. Project stands.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The second omits the 'interest more than zero' guard; with no interest line 1 and line 9 are zero, so the value is the same, and the project's guard keeps a filer without student loan interest from being asked whether they are claimed as a dependent. The eligibility tests (not married filing separately, not claimed as a dependent) agree.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 98, Schedule 1, line 21: "You can take this deduction only if all of the following apply", including "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, aren't claimed as a dependent on someone else's (such as your parent's) 2025 tax return." The reply drops that condition, saying no supplied input states it, but the request's person collection carried person.sav_claimed ("Are you claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return?"), which the project counts in sli.claimed_count. Completed stage11.sli.claimed (project $0, reply $1,200) and stage11.sli.spouse_claimed (project $0, reply $2,497.50). executable triage (.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json, executable-triage-v2): 2,063 of 2,726 agree; 6 value (3 completed), 155 candidate-unknown (20 completed: the reply reads the loan answers without sli.any), 492 candidate-refuses (refused returns, upstream refusals through line 9), 10 project-unknown. Project stands.

Ruling: interface gap; i1040gi p. 98, Schedule 1, line 21 (the conditions for the deduction). The reply's two tests are the project's (a filing status other than married filing separately; no one on the return claimed as a dependent, person.sav_claimed) and it gives worksheet line 9 as the project does. It lacks the project's first alternative, $0 when no interest was paid (sli.interest zero), so it reads person.sav_claimed on returns with no student loan interest. The earlier rulings on this line found earlier replies to lack the dependent test; this reply has it. Re-reviewed because sli.interest was reworded (the older "(or your spouse if filing jointly)" in the eligible-student list is now the one spouse phrase; wording only, no expression changed). executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sli.json`, pass 970c08bc396c; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 40 partial records): 1,759 of 2,307 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-refuses": 331, "candidate-unknown": 208, "project-unknown": 9}; on completed returns 101 candidate-unknown (on the six the record lists the project is $0 and the reply is unknown for person.sav_claimed); no value difference. The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: model error; same point as the earlier rulings on this line. i1040gi p. 98, Line 21, among the conditions for the deduction: "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, aren't claimed as a dependent on someone else's" 2025 tax return. The reply gives worksheet line 9 on every return not married filing separately and has no test that the filer or the spouse is claimed as a dependent (its note says it found no input that asks it; the project reads person.sav_claimed). On completed returns where a person on the return is claimed the project enters zero and the reply the worksheet amount: 4 completed value differences, the recorded witnesses mutation.t2.sli.qss_divisor ($2,045.00 against $0.00; person[taxpayer].sav_claimed yes), stage11.sli.claimed, stage11.sli.spouse_claimed and stage16.sd.line17_no_skips_19.
